what: A text has several gaps. For each gap you choose the best word from a drop-down list.
tests: Reading and writing: using grammar and meaning to choose the right word.

scoring.note: Pearson says the response is judged on your ability to use contextual and grammatical cues.

strategy: Read the whole text once to understand the topic.
For each gap, check the grammar first: does it need a noun, verb, adjective or adverb?
Then check the meaning and common word partners (collocations).
Read the full sentence again with your choice.
example_prompt: The new policy had a significant ____ on traffic. (impact / affect / effective / impacted)

strong.why: A noun is needed after 'significant', and 'have an impact on' is a common partner.

medium.why: Close in meaning, but 'affect' is a verb, so the grammar is wrong.

weak.why: An adjective does not fit after 'a significant'.

mistakes: Choosing by meaning only and ignoring grammar.
Not reading the words after the gap.
Spending too long on one gap.
